newsitem.title: USA: Hearing postponed in National Enquirer libel suit.
newsitem.headline: Hearing postponed in National Enquirer libel suit.

text.p: A hearing on a request by the National Enquirer to dismiss a libel suit filed against it by entertainer Tammy Wynette was postponed Monday.
The U.S. District Court said arguments in the case originally scheduled for Monday would be heard on Feb. 24.

Wynette, whose hit "Stand By Your Man" made her the first woman in country music to sell over a million records, sued the Enquirer and the Star, both tabloids owned by American Media Operations Inc., charging invasion of privacy, defamation and libel.
The suit claimed that the publications bought her medical records following her treatment at a Pittsburgh hospital in 1995 and ran stories about her health that cost her bookings.
In asking for dismissal of the suit the Enquirer said Wynette had given up her right to privacy where her health is concerned through news releases and her autobiography.
